earlier_scan.note: Only Allen & Hurd 1965 Bougainville survey checklist found; no grammar or phonology of Daantanai' located.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur (compiler). n.d. [deposited 1999]. A draft Nasioi Grammar: 'A Nasioi Grammar. (Rautsch [sic], "Anthropos", 1912.)'. 19-page typed and handwritten manuscript, drafting notes compiled by Capell from Rausch 1912 (Die Sprache von Suedost-Bougainville, Anthropos 7), with some Siwai and Uisai examples. Arthur Capell papers, PARADISEC collection AC2, item NSBNAS103. doi:10.4225/72/56eac8a60ec9d.
sources.note: Page 1 gives Rausch's alphabet (vowels i e a o u incl. underlined e and u; consonants k t d s ts nt ns n r(l) p b v mp m nk ng), three allophonic/orthographic remarks, the one accent sentence with two minimal pairs, then numeral classes 1-6. No tone. Nothing on any Nasioi dialect other than Rausch's.
sources.venue: Arthur Capell papers, PARADISEC collection AC2, item NSBNAS103. doi:10.4225/72/56eac8a60ec9d

sources.citation: 大西正幸 [Onishi, Masayuki]. 2011. ナーシオイ語民話テキスト [Naasioi folktale text]. 地球研言語記述論集 3 [RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series 3] (大西正幸・稲垣和也 eds.), 209-243. Kyoto: Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (総合地球環境学研究所). [sections 1-2.1, pp. 209-211: introduction, 'Overview of the Kieta dialect of Naasioi', phonological system; then glossed text]
sources.note: Phoneme inventory (p t~s k '; b~v d~r; m n ng / i e a o u), syllabic nasals word-initially, coda ng and glottal stop, long vowels = VV provisionally; accent said to be complex and unanalysed; texts are written in Hurd's practical orthography without accent marks.
sources.venue: 地球研言語記述論集 3 [RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series 3] (大西正幸・稲垣和也 eds.)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record daan1235 (JSON) and subtree sout3364 / sout3363 / nasi1248
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the language's 'most extensive descriptions' are Lewis 2009 (Ethnologue) and Allen & Hurd 1965, both whose fullest description per Glottolog is only a wordlist; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. Sisters under South Nasioi: Koromira [koro1313].
Stub: 600 speakers (2007), Piruneu' and Warana villages, South Nasioi; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: OLAC. 2023. OLAC resources in and about the Daantanai' language (lni).
sources.note: Catalog only. Lists a single primary resource for lni: PARADISEC AC2-NSBCVOC201 (Allen & Hurd ca 1964 survey report scan) plus Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List records; no language description of any kind.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2013. Daantanai' [lni]. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th edition. Dallas: SIL International. (Internet Archive copy 2013-04-23)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content; no 'Language Resources' listed. Only linguistic remark: 'Language was different from others in Nasioi group but may have converged to be more like Koromira [kqj] or Naasioi [nas].' Confirms the list of works to obtain expectation that Ethnologue cites no further sources.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request 2008-006 (submitted by Conrad Hurd, SIL, 2007-10-01): rename [lni] Lantanai -> Daantanai'. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only phonological remark (p. 2): the name 'is pronounced with a voiced alveolar stop followed by a geminate cluster and ends with a glottal stop'. Hurd states first-hand knowledge (visited Piruneu' and Warana villages; 30 years in Naasioi area) and cites no published sources.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell. 2005. The languages of Bougainville. In Anthony J. Regan & Helga M. Griffin (eds.), Bougainville before the conflict, 31-46. Canberra: Pandanus Books / ANU Press.
sources.note: Silent. Lantanai appears only in the inventory tables (pp. 41-42): 'Lantanai, Kieta District, 300 speakers [SIL 1990]' and 'Lantanai, Koromira, Oune and Simeku are perhaps best considered to constitute dialects of Nasioi'. No phonology of any Bougainville language.

sources.citation: Dunn, Michael, Ger Reesink & Angela Terrill. 2002. The East Papuan languages: a preliminary typological appraisal. Oceanic Linguistics 41(1): 28-62.
sources.note: pronoun and verb-affix typology only; the article has no section on prosody and says nothing about stress or tone for Koromira

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU.
sources.note: bibliographic pointers only: Mueller, Adam 1955 'Dictionnaire nasioi-anglais, with section on Koromira dialect', 191 pp. roneo, c. 4800 entries; Mueller 1955 'Nasioi grammar' TS 25 pp (SIL holds a 49-pp version); Rausch 1912 'Woerterbuch der Nasioi-Sprache mit Einschaltung der Koromira Mundart' TS 217 pp; Rausch n.d. notes; no phonological statement in the bibliography itself

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 783-804. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Does not mention Lantanai. The East Bougainville Stock (Nasioi, Nagovisi, Siwai, Buin) is characterised only as having 'very simple segmental phonologies with small phoneme inventories' (p. 792); the chapter's one stress remark concerns Rotokas (West Bougainville): 'a complex suprasegmental phonology in which length and stress patterns play a part' (p. 800). Nothing usable for Daantanai'.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Allen, Jerry & Conrad Hurd. 1965. Languages of the Bougainville District. Port Moresby: Department of Information and Extension Services (SIL). 56/58 pp. Scan: PARADISEC AC2-NSBCVOC201 (Capell papers), 59 JPEG page scan.
sources.note: The only document that contains Daantanai' (Lantanai) data at all: 1963 lexicostatistic survey wordlists and boundaries map. Glottolog codes it a wordlist or less, so a stress statement is improbable, but it is the one item that must be looked at before declaring the language undescribed; it may carry a transcription convention note (accent marks) for the wordlists.

sources.citation: Allen, Jerry & Conrad Hurd. [1965]. Languages of the Bougainville District. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics / Port Moresby: Department of Information and Extension Services. 56 pp. + fold-out map. Scan: PARADISEC AC2-NSBCVOC201 (Arthur Capell papers), 59 page scan; doi:10.4225/72/56EAC83B4627D.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content at all: preface, classification method (Swadesh-list cognate scoring), language/dialect lists with populations, cognate-percentage tables per language, section 4 inventory of existing materials (for Nasioi: Rausch 1912 dictionary + French grammar typescript, Mueller 1954-55 Nasioi-English dictionary with unfinished Koromira section and 25 pp 'Nasioi Grammar' typescript, mission primers), literacy recommendations, bibliography, village appendix, map. No wordlists are printed, so not even accent marks. The scanned has no occurrence of stress/accent/tone.
